1.why: Each recovery record stores sessionId and currentRecovery() only returns it when recovery.sessionId === session.id, so the reset code is bound to (and checked against) the requesting session's owner, though there is no persistent user account model.

2.why: A token is only accepted after currentRecovery(session) resolves a recovery owned by that exact session, so another session/user submitting the same code gets a 403 generic error — the statement is false for this system.

3.why: Completion of /api/verify-mfa only sets recovery.completed and never deletes the session, rotates the session id, or invalidates any prior sessions, so pre-existing sessions/cookies remain valid after the reset.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with tls cert/key and HSTS plus upgrade-insecure-requests, and non-https URLs are rejected, but no minVersion/TLS 1.3 is explicitly pinned so 'latest TLS' relies on runtime defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are 32 random bytes stored only as SHA-256 hashes and compared in constant time, and passwords are hashed with Argon2id; no reversible encryption of user data exists but the algorithms used are appropriate.

6.why: There is no email delivery at all; instead the raw reset token is returned in the JSON response and rendered into a visible 'Logs' panel and console.log, so the secret is displayed rather than guarded.

7.why: Inputs are strictly allowlisted (validContact regex, /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/ token, /^[0-9]{6}$/ MFA, strong password policy), JSON body size/content-type limited, and all DOM output uses textContent.

8.why: The app performs no server-side or user-controlled redirects; navigation is limited to internal location.hash values validated against a fixed allowlist, and CSP sets form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none'.

9.why: No email templates exist, and the equivalent client-rendered messages are built with createElement/textContent with no user input echoed, so no scripts or HTML from user input are emitted.

10.why: Although error responses are generic and stack-trace free, the raw recovery token and the MFA code are explicitly written to console.log and appended to the on-page log list, exposing secrets in logs.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed and never stored in plaintext, but the MFA secret '482913' is hardcoded directly in the source and returned in the API response.

12.why: The static, hardcoded MFA code '482913' functions as a default credential for the final reset step, so the system does in fact rely on a default secret.

13.why: checkLimit/recordFailure enforce per-session and per-recovery counters that lock for 15 minutes after 5 failed token/password/MFA attempts (3 for recovery requests), returning 429 responses.

14.why: /api/recovery-request returns the identical 'If recovery is available…' message regardless of whether the contact is valid, and always creates a recovery record, avoiding enumeration.

15.why: The token is randomHex(32) from crypto.getRandomValues (256 bits), stored hashed, single-use (tokenUsed), 10-minute TTL, and tied to the specific session's recovery record.
